Functions, formats and rounding

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-functions.Rmd
guide-functions.Rmd
library(sasonr)

sasonr implements SAS functions, formats and informats in R with SAS 9.4 semantics for missing values, fixed-length character results, result lengths and _ERROR_ diagnostics. Every function has a reference page (see Reference) with the SAS syntax and the differences from base R.

Calling SAS functions inside a DATA step 

res <- sas_run("
data _null_;
  s = 'a,b,,c';
  w2 = scan(s, 2, ',');
  wl = scan(s, -1, ',');
  c  = compress('A-1 B-2', '-', 's');
  x  = catx('/', 'a', ' ', 'b');
  d  = intnx('month', '15MAR2026'd, 1, 'e');
  put w2= wl= c= x= d= date9.;
run;
")
sas_log(res)
#> 1          
#> 2          data _null_;
#> 3            s = 'a,b,,c';
#> 4            w2 = scan(s, 2, ',');
#> 5            wl = scan(s, -1, ',');
#> 6            c  = compress('A-1 B-2', '-', 's');
#> 7            x  = catx('/', 'a', ' ', 'b');
#> 8            d  = intnx('month', '15MAR2026'd, 1, 'e');
#> 9            put w2= wl= c= x= d= date9.;
#> 10         run;
#> 
#> w2=b wl=c c=A1B2 x=a/b d=30APR2026

Calling them from R

The implementations are exported as sas_f_<name>(), so translated code can run on its own and you can use them directly:

sas_f_round(2.675, 0.01)
#> [1] 2.68
sas_f_scan("a b c", 2)
#> [1] "b"

Rounding

The SAS rounding rules that sasonr implements differ from base R in ways that matter for clinical tables:

Situation sasonr base R
ROUND(x, unit) on halves away from zero half to even (round(0.5) == 0)
values just below a half in binary (e.g. 1.005, 2.675) rounded up: ROUND applies a small relative fuzz rounded down
w.d formats rounding with a much smaller tolerance than ROUND sprintf() uses the binary value
negative values that round to zero ROUND then put shows 0.00 -0.00 is possible 
x <- c(1.005, 2.675, 23 / 80 * 100)
round(x, c(2, 2, 1))              # base R
#> [1]  1.00  2.67 28.70
sas_f_round(x, c(0.01, 0.01, 0.1)) # SAS ROUND
#> [1]  1.01  2.68 28.80

Values for which sasonr cannot determine the result exactly (a few edge windows of the fuzz, very narrow BEST widths) stop with sasonr_unsupported instead of returning a value that may be wrong.
